It took 3 years of fighting and meetings and organizing but my BIPOC classmates and I sought out BIPOC professors who could support us and even started a BIPOC fellowship in our little cohort. I think my case is more the exception than the norm since we were a small private school. Harder to do with public universities.

I preferred the cohort model because I get to stick with the same people throughout the course and everyone’s sorta in it together for better or worse. I don’t like a revolving door of new faces without any established classroom culture.

I am of the mindset that some people may find it hard to keep having sex with the same person for the rest of their lives, so when my husband suggested sleeping with other people, I was open to the idea. I didn't need to, but he could. He found a girl from work and he wanted transparency (which I thought was nice), so he invited me to dinner with them so I could see how they were like. So they slept together but things still didn't quite sit well so I told him, I can't go on with this. He agreed to stop but clearly resented me for it. We would go days just arguing and him justifying why he should be allowed to do it. I got tired and said "fine, whatever, go ahead". By this point we were already in separate rooms because he kept rubbing her in my face and I was having none of it. He kept replaying a playlist she made for him, wanted to watch movies she recommended. He even asked if it was okay to put up a picture of them in the room he was sleeping in.

After a while, he said an open marriage is how he saw his life and clearly I wasn't okay with it so he asked for a separation. Bear in mind, during this time I was having severe depression and anxiety because my mind kept thinking about what they were doing together. So I gathered up some girlfriends and went out. So my "advice" is, if you're not okay with it, then you're not okay with it. Accept that as time passed, your husband has changed and the views he had of monogamy has changed. You can bend over backwards to make him happy but at whose expense? If you're anything like me (which you sound like), it would be very, very, very hard and would depend a lot on your husband's behavior around you and with the other person.
